test_policy.notes: The international page says ACT or SAT scores are 'not required but should be submitted if available'; the CDS (C8) ticks 'recommended' for SAT or ACT. Admission is based on a combination of the high school core curriculum, ACT and/or SAT composite (if available), GPA and class rank (GPA alone for schools that do not rank). Meeting the minimums does not guarantee admission or admission to a particular program.

requirements.supplemental_essays: Optional personal statement of 500 words or less (educational goals, personal circumstances); not required.
requirements.notes: Apply with the S&T online application or the Common App (submit only one); choose Undergraduate Application / First-Time College Student / Bachelor's and a specific major (do not choose 'Undecided' or 'Undecided Engineering', because the specific program must appear on the I-20). Unofficial transcripts and test scores are accepted for the admission decision; official ones are required after an offer; transcripts must show courses, grades, rank and GPA, and S&T may ask for a WES evaluation (U.S. equivalency only). The application fee comes from the CDS 2025-26 (C13: no application fee); the international page does not mention a fee. The admission application is processed without financial documents, but a statement of financial support (sponsor or bank) is needed before immigration documents are issued. Score codes: ACT 2398, SAT 6876. The page lists no teacher or counselor recommendation requirement. CDS H7 ticks no financial aid form for nonresident first-year applicants.

deadlines.label: Recommended application date, fall 2027 (August start)
deadlines.notes: Admissions are rolling with no firm deadline; applications stay open after the recommended date. The page prints 'Fall Semester (Aug. - Dec.) - April 1' with no year, so April 1, 2027 is assumed for fall 2027 entry. It advises applying well before this date to leave time for I-20 issuance and a visa appointment. The spring (Jan. - May) recommended date is Oct. 1, which has already passed for spring 2027.

english_policy.waiver_notes: All non-native English-speaking international applicants must show English proficiency before enrolling in a degree program. Exempt: applicants from the listed English-speaking countries (e.g. Australia, Canada except Quebec, Ghana, Ireland, Kenya, Nigeria, Singapore, South Africa, United Kingdom, New Zealand; 'applicants from all other countries will need to provide TOEFL, IELTS, PTE, or Duolingo scores') and applicants with a degree from a university in the US, UK, Australia, New Zealand or Canada (except Quebec). Alternatives to a test for full admission: ACT English + Reading 37, SAT ERW 500, IB English 5 on a HL exam, AP English Language 3, IGCSE/GCE O and A level English grade B. Pathway Program: applicants who meet all academic requirements but not the English requirement may be admitted with lower scores (TOEFL 3.5 new scale / 60 old scale for tests before Jan 1, 2026, IELTS 5.5, PTE 50, Duolingo 105, Cambridge 162) and take English 1110 in their first semester; passing it satisfies the requirement. Unofficial scores are accepted.

english.notes: Old 0-120 scale, 'Test taken prior to January 1, 2026: 80'. Pathway Program minimum 60 on this scale.
New 1-6 scale (the page lists 'TOEFL: 4.5' for tests from Jan 1, 2026). Pathway Program minimum 3.5.
B2 First, C1 Advanced or C2 Proficiency score of 176. Pathway Program minimum 162.

aid.notes: Provost's International Merit Scholarship: international first-time freshmen and transfers entering in 2027-28 on a first bachelor's degree receive $15,000 per year (split between fall and spring) with no separate application; generally F-1 students only (others are evaluated at admission), not for company- or government-sponsored students, not combinable with another automatic merit scholarship, and lost on gaining Missouri residency. Renewal needs 12+ hours and a 3.00 cumulative GPA, for up to 8 semesters. The Distinguished Scholars Award and the Out-of-State Groundbreaker scholarships are limited to US citizens and permanent residents. The CDS (H6) ticks both institutional need-based and non-need-based aid for nonresident undergraduates and reports 186 degree-seeking nonresident undergraduates (international and out-of-state US students) receiving institutional aid, average $12,175; the aid pages describe no need-based program for international students, so the policy is entered as merit_only.

tier_notes.engineering: Engineering is the core of the university; the degree list includes uncommon programs such as mining, petroleum, nuclear, ceramic and metallurgical engineering. Placed in the 41-100 band as a judgment, not a cited ranking.
tier_notes.computer_science: Computer science is offered but is not a nationally top-100 program (judgment).
tier_notes.arts_design: No art or design degree (the university's undergraduate degree list has none).
